report.verdict: The posting seeks an engineering manager; your resume shows senior field operations leadership instead.
write_up: This posting is for a different track from your experience: it asks for an engineering manager, while your resume follows your progression through field operations at Northstar Home Services. That progression is clear, but the engineering background the role requires isn't shown.

It's common for senior operations resumes to list broad responsibilities without showing how large the operation was or what changed. That makes it difficult to compare your work with other operations leaders. Your line about partnering with Finance on the annual operating plan is a useful model: it names the partner and the work.

Let's start with your current Northstar role. Add the team and budget figures you can substantiate, then name the initiatives you led and what changed. For this posting, add engineering experience only if you have it; otherwise, your resume points more directly to senior field operations roles.

cards.line: Northstar Home Services has no description of its business or size.
cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter may not know the company or how large its operation is. A short description can give your leadership work a frame.
cards.question: What does Northstar Home Services do, and what company-wide measure of its size can you share?

cards.line: Responsible for field operations, dispatch and customer care across the Upper Midwest
cards.cannot_tell: The functions and geography are clear, but a recruiter can't tell how large your operation was. At senior director level, the people or budget in your remit matter.
cards.example: Responsible for field operations, dispatch and customer care across the Upper Midwest, overseeing [number of employees] and [operating budget]
cards.question: How many employees and what budget were in your remit?

cards.line: Reported to the COO and partnered with Finance on the annual operating plan
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this. It gives a recruiter a concrete business process and shows where you worked with another function.
A recruiter can see two areas you oversaw, but not what you did with either one. Name a decision or change you made.
cards.example: Oversaw vendor management and fleet, including [decision or change]
cards.question: What decision or change did you make in vendor management or fleet?

cards.line: Led operational strategy and continuous improvement initiatives
cards.cannot_tell: The initiatives aren't named, so a recruiter can't tell what you led or what changed. One concrete initiative would give this work weight.
cards.example: Led [initiative] as part of operational strategy and continuous improvement, resulting in [what changed]
cards.question: Which initiative did you lead, and what changed?

cards.cannot_tell: Managing managers is important for this level. The number of managers and what their teams handled would show more of the job.
cards.example: Managed [number] managers across multiple regions whose teams handled [responsibilities]
cards.question: How many managers did you manage, and what did their teams handle?

cards.line: Oversaw technicians and dispatch for the Twin Cities market
cards.cannot_tell: The market and teams are named, but the operation's size is missing. A count of technicians or another measure you tracked would show how much you oversaw.
cards.example: Oversaw [number] technicians and dispatch for the Twin Cities market
cards.question: How many technicians did you oversee in the Twin Cities market?

cards.line: Rolled out a new scheduling system
cards.cannot_tell: The rollout is concrete, but a recruiter can't tell what it involved or what changed after it. Name the system and the result if you can.
cards.example: Rolled out [scheduling system], resulting in [what changed]
cards.question: What scheduling system did you roll out, and what changed afterward?

cards.cannot_tell: First-time fix rate is a useful measure for field service. The line doesn't say how much it improved or what you did to improve it.
cards.example: Improved first-time fix rate from [starting rate] to [ending rate] by [action]
cards.question: What were the starting and ending rates, and what did you do to improve them?

cards.line: Ran daily operations for the service department
cards.cannot_tell: Running daily operations could cover several jobs. Naming the work you handled would distinguish it from the title.
cards.example: Ran daily operations for the service department, including [responsibilities]
cards.question: What were your main responsibilities in the service department's daily operations?

fit.why: Your headline and Northstar roles center on field operations, dispatch, customer care and managing managers.
fit.level: director, current Senior Director role managing managers across multiple regions
fit.note: Your work with Finance and experience managing managers are relevant leadership experience. If you have additional technical experience, describe it with the same concrete dates, roles and responsibilities as the work already listed.

posting.summary: Lead backend engineers responsible for payouts and the ledger, including team development, delivery and production operations.
missing: Manage, hire and develop a team of 6 to 8 engineers, including performance reviews and career growth; 2+ years managing engineers with direct reports, including hiring and performance management
Own the team's roadmap and delivery with your product partner
Run the team's operations: on-call health, incident reviews and planning; Experience leading teams that run production systems with on-call
Build relationships with Finance, Risk and Support
5+ years of backend engineering before moving into management
A record of growing engineers into senior roles
